alignments.note: Second attributive article before a verbless genitive modifier for which the ASV supplies no relative clause at all; rule 31's closing clause leaves it empty.
Rule 21: the case preposition rides with the article, headed on 'the'.

Substantival article before a participle supplies the pronoun and nothing else under rule 32; the case preposition rides with it, realizing the article's own dative. No other source token competes for the pronoun here, which is what distinguishes this unit from s012.
The ASV writes no word for the correlative particle, so rule 70 leaves it empty; the answering δέ keeps its own 'but'.
Participle keeps the relativizer as its helper under rule 32; head on the verb word.
Predicate noun standing bare, the Greek copula being expressed.
Expressed copula, fronted in English under rule 15.

The article realizes nothing: ἡμῖν stands in apposition and has already written the antecedent 'us', so no pronoun is left for it, and rule 32's 'and nothing else' leaves it with no other word to take, the participle being what the relative clause is predicated of. This is rule 20's stated contrast, Ὑμῖν ... τοῖς ἔθνεσιν -> 'to you that are Gentiles', and it is the reading 1CO.1.24 takes for the identical apposition αὐτοῖς δὲ τοῖς κλητοῖς. Rule 90's single-word arm does not apply, the ASV writing 'who are saved' for the pair. Giving the article the relativizer 'who' and leaving the participle 'are saved' remains defensible and was this verse's earlier reading, but it is not what the chapter does at 1.24. A reference comparison will report this as a disagreement and that report is not a correction.

Participle recast as a finite relative clause takes the relativizer and the supplied copula as rule 7 and 9 helpers, the article having no pronoun left to supply; rule 17 heads on the lexical verb rather than the copula. This is the analysis 1CO.1.24 gives κλητοῖς -> 'that are called'.

Dative pronoun with its case preposition riding along under rule 21's determinerless clause; head on the pronoun. This pronoun is the antecedent the relative clause is predicated of, which is why the article at s012 has nothing left to supply.
Greek is anarthrous, so the supplied 'the' is a rule 51 helper on the noun.
Genitive rendered 'of + noun'; head on the noun.
Expressed copula with the expletive subject English requires.

review_notes: s012 is brought into line with 1CO.1.24's τοῖς κλητοῖς: an expressed pronoun standing in apposition has already written the antecedent, so the article has no pronoun left to supply and the participle carries the relativizer.

s007 is untouched and is the contrast within this same verse: there no pronoun stands in apposition, so the article takes 'to them' under rule 32 and the participle takes 'that perish'. The two units now differ only in what the source expresses.
Rule 90 was considered and does not apply: it relaxes rule 32 only where the ASV writes a single English word for the article and participle together, and here it writes 'who are saved'.
A reference comparison will now report s012 as a disagreement with BSB. That report is not a correction; it is the same convention BSB already disagrees with at 1CO.1.24.
